full_text.Title: Poly(2,6-dimethyl-1,4-phenylene oxide) containing imidazolium-terminated long side chains as hydroxide exchange membranes with improved conductivity

Sections.name: Introduction
content: Hydroxide exchange membrane fuel cells (HEMFCs) have received growing interest because of their advantages over proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) [1]. Operating in the alkaline environment, HEMFCs exhibit enhanced kinetics of both the fuel oxidation and oxygen reduction, which allow non-precious metals to be used as active catalysts (e.g. silver and nickel) . In addition, the catalysts could be more stable in the basic medium than in the acidic one. Therefore, HEMFCs have the potential to solve the problems of catalyst cost and durability while achieving high power and energy density [4].

As a critical component in HEMFCs, hydroxide exchange membranes (HEMs) serve as both hydroxide conductors and fuel/oxidant separators simultaneously, controlling HEMFCs' performance [5]. HEMs possess lower conductivities compared to proton exchange membranes (PEMs), due to the intrinsically lower mobility of hydroxide ions compared to protons [6]. Thus many efforts have been made aiming to develop highly conductive HEMs. The most frequently used route is grafting hydroxide conducting groups onto the high-performance polymers. Poly(2,6-dimethyl-1,4-phenylene oxide) (PPO) has extensive applications in hydroxide exchange membranes (HEMs), due to its excellent physicochemical properties including good mechanical strength, thermal stability and chemical stability . PPO based HEM materials are commonly prepared via introducing halogenomethyl groups onto PPO polymer matrix, followed by the functionalization reaction . As the functional groups are connected to the PPO backbone via short links, it is hard to form good hydrophilic/hydrophobic micro-phase separation structure which is necessary for well-interconnected hydroxide transporting pathways. Therefore, the PPO based membranes prepared by this method showed low hydroxide conductivity.

There are two approaches which could enhance the hydroxide conductivity of HEMs: increasing the ion exchange capacity (IEC) and improving the ionic mobility [14]. Higher IEC could offer the ability to absorb more water uptake, which make hydroxide conducting channels more connected, thus enhancing hydroxide conductivity . However, high water uptake inevitably expands the overall hydrophilic domains, and eventually induces excessive swelling of these membranes, even loss of dimension stability . Crosslinking is usually applied in the design of polymer architecture to obtain mechanically robust HEMs with improved dimensional stability [20]. However, the degree of crosslinking is usually not easily controlled. Hence an effective strategy to boost hydroxide conductivity of HEMs is to improve the hydroxide mobility by promoting hydrophilic/hydrophobic micro-phase separation structure to construct hydroxide conducting highway [21]. Enhancing the mobility of functional groups by introducing long side chains [22] and designing a natural aggregation of functional groups by introducing multiple functional groups in one side chain could enhance the micro-phase separation ability of PPO based HEMs. Compared to multiple functionalization, the synthetic processes of introducing long side chains are easier to be controlled, but still need harsh reaction conditions.

Herein, a novel PPO with imidazolium terminated long side chains was synthesized by simple and controllable acetylation reaction of PPO under moderate reaction conditions (at room temperature), followed by a Menshutkin reaction with 1,2-dimethylimidazole. Compared to the literatures [22], the reaction condition used here is much more mild. The effects of long side chains on water uptake, swelling ratio, hydroxide conductivity, thermal and alkaline stability for the membranes were comprehensively investigated. The introduction of the flexible long side chain enhances the mobility of the terminated imidazolium groups, promoting the formation of hydrophilic/hydrophobic micro-phase separation structure. Given similar swelling ratios, the long side chain type PPO membrane exhibits much higher hydroxide conductivity than the short side chain type one.

content.name: Materials
content: Poly(2,6-dimethyl-1,4-phenylene oxide) (PPO, GFN2-701) was obtained from SABIC Innovative Plastics (USA), with a molecular weight of about 50,000. Chloromethyl octyl ether (CMOE) was synthesized according to the Ref. [24]. Aluminum chloride anhydrous, tin chloride anhydrous, 6-bromohexanoyl chloride, 1,2-dimethylimidazole, n-octanol, polyoxymethylene, calcium chloride anhydrous, hydrochloric acid (37–38%), ethanol, and N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) were commercially obtained and used as received without further purification. All the used chemicals in the experiments were analytical grade. Dichloromethane and chloroform was dried over molecular sieves (4 Å, 8–12 mesh) before use. In order to reduce the possible effect of CO_{2} dissolved in deionized water on the membrane characterization, the deionized water was boiled to completely degassed prior to use.

content.name: Preparation of long-side-chain imidazolium functionalized PPO membranes
content: A long side chain was grafted onto the PPO by the acetylation reaction of PPO and 6-bromohexanoyl chloride. 1 g PPO was dissolved in 10 mL dichloromethane to form a PPO solution in a 25 mL round-bottom flask with strenuous stirring. 0.67 g of aluminum chloride anhydrous was added into 15 mL dichloromethane with stirring in a three-neck flask under nitrogen. The flask was chilled in an ice/water bath, then 0.77 mL 6-bromohexanoyl chloride was added dropwise into the stirring solution. After that, the PPO solution was added into the flask, and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature for 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, and 3 h. The final PPO containing bromide terminated long side chains (PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Br) was obtained by depositing the reaction solution in ethanol and the solid was dried at room temperature under vacuum.

Long-side-chain imidazolium functionalized PPO was prepared from the reaction between PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Br and 1,2-dimethylimidazole. 0.76 g PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Br and 3 equivalents 1,2-dimethylimidazole were dissolved into 12 mL NMP with stirring, then the solution was heated to 80 °C and kept for 24 h. After cooling to room temperature, the solution was filtered and poured onto a glass casting plate. After curing and drying at 80 °C for 48 h, the long-side-chain imidaozlium functionalized PPO (PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im) membrane was obtained and peeled off the glass plate. The final PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membranes in OH^{−} form were immersed in 1 M KOH solution at room temperature for 24 h to exchange the ion from Br^{−} to OH^{−}. The resulted membranes were washed and immersed with deionized water until neutral. The synthetic processes are shown in Fig. 1.

content.name: Preparation of short-side-chain imidazolium functionalized PPO membranes
content: Short-side-chain imidazolium functionalized PPO was synthesized by the typical two-step chloromethylation-functionalization method. The synthetic procedures illustrated in Fig. 2. 1 g of PPO was added to 50 mL chloroform at room with stirring, followed by addition of 0.05 mL anhydrous tin chloride and CMOE (1, 1.5, 2, and 2.5 mL, respectively). The reaction was kept at room temperature for 30 min. The final chloromethylated PPO (PPO-CH_{2}-Cl) was obtained by depositing the reaction solution in ethanol and drying at room temperature under vacuum. Then, 0.9 g PPO-CH_{2}-Cl was dissolved into 12.8 mL NMP with stirring, followed by adding twice stoichiometric 1,2-dimethylimidazole. The reaction was kept at 80 °C for 24 h. The solution was cast onto a glass plate and kept in an oven at 80 °C for 48 h, and then the short-side-chain imidazolium functionalized PPO (PPO-CH_{2}-Im) membrane was peeled off the glass plate. The final PPO-CH_{2}-Im membranes in OH^{−} form were obtain by immersion of the membrane in 1 M KOH solution at room temperature for 24 h, followed by washing and immersion with deionized water until neutral.

content.name: ^{1}H NMR
content: ^{1}H NMR spectroscopy confirmed the acylation, chloromethylation of PPO and the later functionalization; it was also used to determine the degree of acylation and chloromethylation of PPO. ^{1}H NMR spectra were recorded on a Bruker AVANCE III HD 500 spectrometer at a resonance frequency of 500 MHz using CDCl_{3} or DMSO-d_{6} as the solvent. Tetramethylsilane (TMS) was used as an internal standard in all cases. The degree of acylation (DA) of PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Brs was calculated from the ^{1}H NMR peak areas: DA=3A(H_{7})/A(H_{2}), where A(H_{7}) and A(H_{2}) are the integral area of the H_{7} peak and H_{2} peak in Fig. 2, respectively. The degree of chloromethylation (DC) of PPO-CH_{2}-Cls was calculated from the NMR peak areas: DC=3A(H_{c})/A(H_{b}), where A(H_{c}) and A(H_{b}) are the integral area of the H_{c} peak and H_{b} peak in Fig. 3, respectively.

content.name: Ion exchange capacity (IEC)
content: The IEC of the membranes in hydroxide form was measured by back titration. The membrane sample was equilibrated with 0.01 M HCl standard solution for 24 h, followed by back titration of 0.01 M NaOH standard solution with phenolphthalein as the indicator. The measured IEC_{m} (mmol g^{−1}) of the membrane was calculated by the Eq. content.name: Water uptake and swelling ratio
content: The membrane samples were immersed in deionized water at different temperatures for more than 12 h to ensure the full hydration. The membrane surfaces were quickly wiped dry with tissue paper, and then the weights and dimensions of wet membranes were measured. The weights and dimensions of dry membranes were obtained after the wet membranes were dried for 24 h at 60 °C in vacuum. The water uptake and swelling ratio could be calculated using the Eqs. , respectively: where W _{wet} and W _{dry} are weights of wet and dry membrane samples, respectively. L _{wet} and L _{dry} are the logarithmic mean length of wet and dry membrane samples, respectively.

content.name: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA)
content: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analyses of PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im and PPO-CH_{2}-Im membranes were used to investigate the micro-phase separated morphology of the membranes on a JEOL JEM-2000EX microscope. The membrane was dyed with PdCl_{4} ^{2−} by immersing in a PdCl_{2}/HCl solution for 2 days, followed by washing with water and then drying at room temperature for 12 h [2]. SAXS analysis of the membranes was carried out by using PANalytical X′Pert Powder X-ray diffraction equipment. The intensity of the X-ray scattering was plotted versus the scattering vector, q, defined as 4πsinθ/λ, where λ is the X-ray wavelength of 0.154 nm. Thermal stabilities of PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im and PPO-CH_{2}-Im were tested by a thermogravimetric analyzer (Mettler Toledo TGA/SDTA851^{e}). About 10 mg sample was heated from 100 °C to 800 °C at a heating rate of 10 °C min^{−1} under an air atmosphere. The samples were dried for 24 h at 50 °C in vacuum to remove moisture prior to the test.

content.name: Hydroxide conductivity
content: The hydroxide conductivity of the membranes was measured in deionized water by a typical four-electrode AC impedance method, using Ivium-n-Stat equipment as the impedance analyzer from 1 to 10^{5} Hz. The hydroxide conductivity, σ, of the membrane was calculated using the Eq. (4):where L is the distance between the two potential electrodes (1 cm here), d and W are the thickness and width of the membrane sample, respectively, and R is the high frequency resistance.

content.name: Alkaline stability
content: Alkaline stabilities of the PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-ImOH and PPO-CH_{2}-ImOH membranes were investigated by measuring hydroxide conductivity after exposure of the membranes to 1 mol L^{−1} KOH aqueous solution at 60 °C for different times. Prior to the conductivity test, the membranes were washed with deionized water to remove the residue KOH and immersed in deionized water for at least 48 h with the water replaced several times. The hydroxide conductivity was measured in 20 °C water.

content.name: Hydrogen/oxygen permeability
content: Pure gas permeation of the membrane was measured in a permeation cell, and the effective permeation membrane area is 9.61 cm^{2} at room temperature. The feed side was maintained at a constant pressure at 0.15 MPa, and the permeation side of the membrane was set at the atmospheric pressure. Before entering the permeation cell, the feed gas was fully humidified. Gas permeance was measured by a soap bubble flow meter.

content.name: Mechanical property
content: The tensile strength and elongation-to-break of the hydrated membranes were obtained with a SANS mechanical analyzer in an air atmosphere at room temperature with the cross-head speed of 5 mm min^{−1}. Dumbbell-shaped membrane samples were tailored following the international standard ISO 527.

content.name: Structure confirmation
content: ^{1}H NMR spectra of PPO and PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Br are presented in Fig. 3(a). In the ^{1}H NMR spectrum of pristine PPO, H_{1} peak has a chemical shift (6.47 ppm, protons on phenyl groups), and H_{2} peak has a chemical shift (2.09 ppm, protons on methyl groups). After the acylation, PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Br spectrum shows six new groups of peaks: 6.07 ppm (H_{1′}), 2.98 ppm (H_{3}), 1.78 ppm (H_{4}), 1.52 ppm (H_{5}), 1.89 ppm (H_{6}), and 3.39 ppm (H_{7}), confirming the successful synthesis of PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Br. H1′ has a greater chemical shift, due to the negative induction effect of carbonyl groups. As shown in Fig. 3(b), the characteristic imidazolium-related proton bands at 2.56, 3.73, and 7.62 ppm are assigned to the proton signals of NC(CH_{3})N (H_{8}), NCH_{3} (H_{9}) and NCHCHN (H_{10}, H_{11}), respectively, indicating the successful incorporation of imidazolium groups. The proton signals in the imidazolium switch down compared to 1,2-dimethylimidazole, because the electron density of imidazole rings is decreased by direct linking with electron-withdrawing positively-charged nitrogen atom. The degrees of acylation (DAs) of PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Brs synthesized here are 24%, 33%, 38%, and 44%, respectively. The IECs of corresponding PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membranes were calculated from ^{1}H NMR spectra to be 1.41, 1.74, 1.90, and 2.07, respectively. The IECs obtained by titration are 1.16, 1.31, 1.53, and 1.83 mmol g^{−1}, respectively. The values of titration IECs are lower than those of NMR-derived IECs.

Fig. 3(c) shows ^{1}H NMR spectra of PPO and PPO-CH_{2}-Cl. After the chloromethylation, a new characteristic peak of the protons in –CH_{2}Cl appears at 4.92 ppm (H_{c}). After the Menshutkin reaction between PPO-CH_{2}-Cl and 1, 2-dimethylimidazole, all proton signals in imidazole rings of PPO polymer main-chain slightly shifted downfield as shown in Fig. 3(d). The proton bands at 2.68, 3.79, 7.20, and 7.70 ppm are assigned to the proton signals of NC(CH_{3})N (H_{d}), NCH_{3} (H_{e}) and NCHCHN (H_{f}, H_{g}) in imidazolium groups, respectively, indicating the successful synthesis of PPO-CH_{2}-Im. The degrees of chloromethylation (DCs) of PPO-CH_{2}-Cls synthesized here are 19%, 24%, 27%, and 34%, respectively. The IECs of corresponding PPO-CH_{2}-Im membranes were calculated from ^{1}H NMR spectra to be 1.32, 1.60, 1.75, and 2.04, respectively. The IECs obtained by titration are 1.14, 1.36, 1.52, and 1.68 mmol g^{−1}, respectively. The values of titration IECs are also lower than those of NMR-derived IECs.

content.name: Morphology
content: The hydrophilic/hydrophobic micro-phase separation structure is of particular importance for HEMs to build effective hydroxide ion conductive channels [25]. The TEM images of PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im (IEC: 1.83 mmol g^{−1}) and PPO-CH_{2}-Im (IEC: 1.68 mmol g^{−1}) membranes are shown in Fig. 4. In order to investigate micro-phase separation and ionic aggregation, membranes are stained with Pd^{2+} [2]. The dark and bright areas correspond to regions of hydrophilic species and hydrophobic species, respectively. As shown in Fig. 4(a), the dispersed small ionic clusters are observed for PPO-CH_{2}-Im membrane. In contrast, bigger ionic clusters and more continuous hydrophilic domains are illustrated for PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membrane in Fig. 4(b). Furthermore, SAXS was used to study the micro-phase separation morphology of hydrated membranes. SAXS patterns of PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im (IEC: 1.83 mmol g^{−1}) and PPO-CH_{2}-Im (IEC: 1.68 mmol g^{−1}) membranes are shown in Fig. 5. The Bragg spacing, d, can be calculated by the equation: d=2π/q, and the ionomer peaks are ascribed to the interparticle scattering from ionic domains according to literature [26]. The PPO-CH_{2}-Im membrane shows a weak scattering reflection with an average interparticle dimension of 11 nm. In comparison, PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membrane exhibits a peak with a larger average interparticle dimension of 15 nm, indicating a larger interspacing dimension of ionic clusters. This is consistent with TEM images (Fig. 4). Besides, the scattering peak of PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membrane is much sharper than that of PPO-CH_{2}-Im membrane. TEM images indicate that the hydrophilic/hydrophobic micro-phase separation structure is better for PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membrane than for PPO-CH_{2}-Im membrane. The introduction of flexible long side chains improves the mobility of the terminated functional groups, promotes the aggregation of hydrophilic species, thus leading to the formation of continuous hydrophilic ionic domains. In addition, the long side chain keeps the hydrophobic PPO main-chain away from the hydrophilic groups, facilitating the assembly of continuous hydrophobic domains. Both of them enhances the hydrophilic/hydrophobic micro-phase separation in PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membranes. Therefore, a better hydrophilic/hydrophobic micro-phase separation structure is built in the PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membranes.

content.name: Water uptake, swelling ratio and mechanical properties
content: Water uptake and swelling ratio have great effects on hydroxide conductivity and dimensional stability of the membranes. The membrane has to absorb enough water for constructing continuous hydroxide conducting channels, while too much water would cause excessive swelling of the membrane. Water uptake and swelling ratio for all the membranes have no change as the temperature increases from 20 to 60 °C. Water uptake and swelling ratio at 60 °C are show in Fig. 6. Both water uptake and swelling ratio expectedly increase with the increase of IEC. Increasing IEC would make the ion clusters larger and hydrophilic channels easier to be continuous, which inevitably expands the overall hydrophilic domains and thus induces more water uptake and larger swelling ratio [27]. All the membranes are robust and their swelling ratio are no more than 32%. At all IECs, PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membranes exhibit a little higher water uptake and swelling ratio compared to PPO-CH_{2}-Im membranes. The long side-chain membranes have segregation of the hydrophilic domains from the hydrophobic polymer main-chain, which may enhance the water uptake to a certain extent [28]. Essentially, IEC determines the water uptake and swelling ratio of the PPO based membranes prepared here. The effect of swelling ratio on mechanical properties are shown in Fig. 7. With increasing swelling ratio, the tensile strength decreases, and the elongation-to-break increases for both PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im and PPO-CH_{2}-Im membranes. The PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membrane shows longer elongation-to-break than PPO-CH_{2}-Im membrane with similar swelling ratios. It suggests that the introduction of the long side chain improved the flexibility of the membrane.

content.name: Hydroxide conductivity
content: Hydroxide conductivity is crucial for the membranes in the fuel cell application. Essentially, IEC has a great effect on hydroxide conductivity of the membrane. Hydroxide conductivity of PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im and PPO-CH_{2}-Im membranes with different IECs at 20 °C are shown in Fig. 8. The hydroxide conductivity for both of them increases with increasing IEC, due to the formation of more interconnected hydrophilic channels with the increase in water uptake. At a certain IEC, PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membranes show higher hydroxide conductivity than PPO-CH_{2}-Im membranes do. e.g., PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membrane with IEC of 1.53 mmol g^{−1} has hydroxide conductivity of 34 mS cm^{−1} that is much higher than that of PPO-CH_{2}-Im membrane (18 mS cm^{−1} at IEC of 1.52 mmol g^{−1}). The hydroxide conductivity of PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im with IEC of 1.83 mmol g^{−1} is up to 42 mS cm^{−1}, which is higher than that of ammonium functionalized PPO containing semi-flexible –pH(CH_{2})_{3}– spacer chains (27 mS cm^{−1}) [29] and comparable to that of ammonium functionalized PPO containing fully-flexible –(CH_{2})_{5}– spacer chains (44 mS cm^{−1}) [22]. It suggests that increasing the flexibility of spacer chains would benefit the hydroxide conduction of the membranes.

The concentration of hydroxide ion ([N^{+}OH^{−}]) in the membrane was calculated by the equation, [N^{+}OH^{−}]=n OH^{−}/V _{wet}, where n is n _{O} H^{−} is the amount of hydroxide ion and V _{wet} is the volume of the hydrated membrane. As shown in Fig. 9(a), the [N^{+}OH^{−}] for PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membrane is the same as that of PPO-CH_{2}-Im membrane. The effective mobility of hydroxide ion was calculated by the equation, σ=F[N^{+}OH^{−}]μ_{OH⁻, eff}, where σ is the hydroxide conductivity, F is Faraday’s constant, [N^{+}OH^{−}] is the concentration of the hydroxide ion, and μOH^{−}, eff is the effective mobility of the hydroxide ion, as described in our previous work [30]. As shown in Fig. 9(b), the effective mobility of the hydroxide ion increases with increasing IEC. The hydroxide effective mobility of PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membranes (2.76–4.85×10^{4} cm^{2} s^{−1} V^{−1}) is almost 2-fold that of PPO-CH_{2}-Im membranes (1.48–2.48×10^{4} cm^{2} s^{−1} V^{−1}). The high conductivity and effective mobility of PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membrane could be attributed to interconnected hydroxide conducting channels derived from good hydrophilic/hydrophobic micro-phase structure.

The original intention of this work is to improve the hydroxide conductivity of HEMs without the challenge of excessive swelling by improving the hydrophilic/hydrophobic phase segregation structure. Fig. 10 shows the hydroxide conductivity of PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im and PPO-CH_{2}-Im membranes as a function of swelling ratio. Hydroxide conductivity increases with the increase in swelling ratio for both PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im and PPO-CH_{2}-Im membranes, due to increasing IEC as well as water uptake. Given similar swelling ratios, the PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membranes exhibit much higher conductivity than PPO-CH_{2}-Im membranes. e.g., PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membrane with swelling ratio of 25% has hydroxide conductivity of 62 mS cm^{−1} (at 60 °C) that is nearly 50% higher than that of PPO-CH_{2}-Im membrane (42 mS cm^{−1} at swelling ratio of 27%). These results clearly verified that the mobility of functional moieties plays a crucial role on achieving high performance HEMs, by promoting the aggregation of hydrophilic segment to result in well-defined phase segregation and inter-connected ion conducting channels.

In addition, hydrogen (fuel) and oxygen (oxidant) permeabilities crossover PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im and PPO-CH_{2}-Im membranes were measured by using the gas permeation measurement equipment as described in our previous work [31]. No gas permeation could be detected for both of them, which suggests the membranes have extremely high hydroxide/oxygen permselectivity.

content.name: Thermal and alkaline stability
content: TGA curves of the PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im (IEC: 1.83 mmol g^{−1}) and PPO-CH_{2}-Im (IEC: 1.68 mmol g^{−1}) are shown in Fig. 11. The thermal decomposition processes are presented by the corresponding thermal characteristic temperatures: the onset decomposition temperatures (T _{OD}s) and the fastest decomposition temperatures (T _{FD}s). The PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im has two weight loss steps. The first step (T _{OD}: 227 °C, T _{FD1}: 242 °C) is attributed to the decomposition of the branched chain. The second step (T_{FD2} of 400 °C) is mainly due to the decomposition of PPO polymer main-chain. The PPO-CH_{2}-Im also has similar two weight loss steps, and its T _{OD} is 176 °C. It is noticed that the onset decomposition temperature is higher for PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im than for PPO-CH_{2}-Im. It suggests that the introduction of long side chain could improve the thermal stability of the membrane.

The alkaline stability for PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im (IEC: 1.83 mmol g^{−1}) and PPO-CH_{2}-Im (IEC: 1.68 mmol g^{−1}) membranes at different time was studied by the changes of normalized hydroxide conductivity (σ_{after}/σ_{before}) and (IEC_{after}/IEC_{before}). As shown in Fig. 12(a), the σ_{after}/σ_{before} of both PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im and PPO-CH_{2}-Im membranes dramatically decrease as a function of immersion time. As shown in Fig. 12(b), IECs for both PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im and PPO-CH_{2}-Im membranes decrease with different immersing time. IEC for the PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membrane suffered a more serious reduction than that for the PPO-CH_{2}-Im membrane, which is consistent with the trend for the change of hydroxide conductivity. After the immersion in 1 M KOH at 60 °C for 120 h, all the membranes remained robust, suggesting a good alkaline stability of PPO main chains. It is quite clear that the decrease in hydroxide conductivity of short-side-chain PPO-CH_{2}-Im membrane due to the poor alkaline stability for imidazolium functional groups. For PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membrane, the imidazolium groups linked to long alkyl chains are stable as described in Ref. [32]. The reason for the instability of PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im might be the decomposition of carbonyl groups in the side chain caused by hydroxides' attack at the carbonyl groups [33].

The alkaline stability of PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im are further investigated by comparing the energy level of the unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO), since the lower the LUMO energy of the compound is, the easier the OH^{−} attack will be. Here, the LUMO energy levels of four model compounds were simulated via density functional theory (B3LYP/6-311G(d,p)) calculations . As shown in Fig. 13, the LUMO energies of [PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im]^{+}, [PPO-C_{6}H_{12}-Im]^{+}, PPO-COC_{5}H_{11} and [PPO-CH_{2}-Im]^{+} were −1.276,−0.922,−1.245 and −0.980 eV, respectively. The LUMO energy of [PPO-C_{6}H_{12}-Im]^{+} is higher than that of [PPO-CH_{2}-Im]^{+}, suggesting that the introduction of long alkyl chains between imidazolium groups and PPO polymer main chain improves the alkaline stability. [PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im]^{+} and PPO-COC_{5}H_{11} have similar LUMO energies, and the LUMO energy is much lower for [PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im]^{+} than for [PPO-C_{6}H_{12}-Im]^{+}. These indicates that the carbonyl groups are more easily attacked by hydroxide ion compared to imidazolium groups. The degradation mechanism of carbonyl groups is not clear so far. Although the alkaline stability is unsatisfied, the long side chain imidazolium functionalized PPO membrane prepared here demonstrates highly enhanced hydroxide conductivity without sacrificing the dimensional stability.

Sections.name: Conclusions
content: A novel poly(2,6-dimethyl-1,4-phenylene oxide) with imidazolium terminated long side chains (PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im) was synthesized by simple and controllable acetylation reaction of PPO and 6-bromohexanoyl chloride in the moderate reaction condition (at room temperature), followed by a Menshutkin reaction with 1,2-dimethylimidazole. The introduction of long chain between imidaozlium groups and polymer main chains facilitate the formation of good hydrophilic/hydrophobic micro-phase separation structure as shown in TEM image. Given similar swelling ratios (25% vs. 27%), long side chain imidazolium functionalized PPO membrane shows much higher conductivity than short side chain one (62 vs. 42 mS cm^{−1}) at 60 °C. It indicates that the PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membranes prepared here exhibits highly enhanced conductivity without sacrificing dimensional stability. The PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membrane shows better flexibility than PPO-CH_{2}-Im membrane. Unfortunately, the alkaline stability for the PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membrane was not improved compared to the PPO-CH_{2}-Im membrane. The LUMO energy level of four model compounds was simulated via density functional theory. [PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im]^{+} has the lowest LUMO energy, suggesting that the carbonyl groups are more easily attacked by hydroxide ion compared to imidazolium groups. Although the alkaline stability is unsatisfied, the long side chain imidazolium functionalized PPO membrane exhibits highly enhanced hydroxide conductivity without scarifying dimensional stability.

full_text.Abstract: Hydroxide exchange membrane fuel cells (HEMFCs) receive growing interest due to the usability of non-precious metal catalysts in the basic operating environment. The applications of HEMFCs are hindered by the trade-off between high hydroxide conductivity and good dimensional stability of the HEMs. Here, a novel poly(2,6-dimethyl-1,4-phenylene oxide) with imidazolium-terminated long side chains (PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im) was synthesized by simple and controllable acetylation reaction of PPO and 6-bromohexanoyl chloride in a moderate condition (at room temperature), followed by the Menshutkin reaction with 1,2-dimethylimidazole. The introduction of long chains between imidazolium groups and polymer main chains facilitates the formation of good hydrophilic/hydrophobic micro-phase separation structure, which is illustrated by TEM. The hydroxide effective mobility in PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membrane is almost 2-fold that in short side chain imidazolium functionalized PPO (PPO-CH_{2}-Im) membrane at a certain IEC. Given similar swelling ratios (25% vs. 27%), PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membrane shows much higher hydroxide conductivity than PPO-CH_{2}-Im membrane (62 vs. 42 mS cm^{−1}) at 60 °C. It indicates that the PPO-COC_{5}H_{10}-Im membranes prepared here exhibits highly enhanced conductivity without sacrificing the dimensional stability.
